external_entities.name: Node Operator
external_entities.description: Human operator configuring whether to enable client identity disclosure
external_entities.rationale: Node operators are external parties making configuration decisions. While typically benign, their configurations affect security posture and privacy exposure.

external_entities.name: P2P Peer Node
external_entities.description: Remote Ethereum node providing ENR records or announcing transactions via devp2p protocols
external_entities.rationale: Network peers can be malicious, send falsified client information, or announce invalid transactions. All peer communications must be validated.

external_entities.name: Malicious Peer
external_entities.description: Attacker node sending falsified client identity information
external_entities.rationale: Explicitly modeled adversary attempting to exploit self-reported client information for targeting attacks or evading detection.

external_entities.name: Contract Caller
external_entities.description: External party executing contract code that uses EXP opcode
external_entities.rationale: Any external party can submit transactions that execute EXP-heavy code. Before EIP-160, attackers could exploit underpriced EXP for DoS attacks.

boundary_interactions.interaction: Implicit: submits transaction executing EXP opcode

external_entities.name: DoS Attacker
external_entities.description: Malicious party attempting to disrupt network via computational DoS using underpriced opcodes
external_entities.rationale: Explicitly modeled adversary exploiting gas mispricing to cause disproportionate computational load relative to gas paid.

external_entities.name: Provider Peer
external_entities.description: Peer claiming to have full blob data in sparse blobpool protocol
external_entities.rationale: Provider peers may withhold data selectively or fail to serve noise columns honestly. Noise-based detection mechanism required to identify misbehavior.

trust_boundary_edges.validation_required: RLP decoding, ASCII validation, client key format validation
Mark data as untrusted, prevent security-critical usage
Gas cost calculation, gas availability check
Post-fork: 5x gas cost increase mitigates DoS viability
Cell mask format validation, transaction hash validation
Noise column presence check, EIP-7594 data validation

coverage_analysis.notes: Cancun system instructions (CREATE/CREATE2, CALL variants, SELFDESTRUCT, RETURN/REVERT) have no external entities - they model internal EVM execution semantics.

security_observations.observation: EIP-7636 client identity is self-reported and inherently untrustworthy - must not be used for security decisions
security_observations.mitigation: Mark client data as untrusted, use only for non-critical network analytics

security_observations.observation: EIP-160 addressed EXP underpricing (4-8x) that enabled computational DoS attacks
security_observations.mitigation: 5x gas increase for EXP byte cost (10 -> 50 gas per byte)

security_observations.observation: EIP-8070 sparse blobpool requires noise column injection to detect selective withholding attacks
security_observations.mitigation: C_extra=1 random noise column in each request, flag peers failing noise checks

security_observations.observation: Sparse blobpool has open TBD items for eclipse attacks and RBF interactions
security_observations.mitigation: Incomplete - marked as open security risks requiring further analysis
